anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 mine has four directly exposed diamond targets in one 5x5x3 rendered voxel pile, with one visible lava hazard and one fragile support in its baseline. Its actual UI and grader require depth-sorted 3D ray hits, camera rotation, material-dependent mining, and finite pick durability, but the baseline has no sealed-target dependency. After Hours at the Reliquary is a 2D fixed-view puzzle without raycast physics or tool durability, yet its current profile adds six views, clue discovery, two inventory recipes, and three dependent wards. That places the reliquary above this L1 on planning, exploration, and memory despite being less demanding in 3D control.

evidence.explanation: The approved mine baseline is difficulty 1 with one screen, one lava block, one support, four targets, and sealed_targets false; both input modes are implemented.
The mine generator builds voxel targets, blockers, optional screens, hazards, and a solution sequence, while explicitly rejecting a layout in which all targets are initially visible.
The approved grader independently raycasts the clicked face, replays material outcomes and durability, and passes only after all diamonds are extracted without collapse.
The assigned current profile has six views, three wards, two-piece combined construction, and unmarked cues.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board has three ordered lamps, three walls, and three wells; its full mode continuously drags an analog knob while a live physics loop applies momentum, collisions, and hazard resets. The reliquary baseline instead has static synchronous scene changes and edge-arrow turns, but requires more cross-view inventory planning and clue memory. Both have a concrete multi-stage medium problem, with the gyroscope harder in continuous temporal and motor control and the reliquary harder in latent-affordance exploration; this supports, rather than proves, the assigned L3.

evidence.explanation: The approved L3 configuration is full interaction with three lamps, three walls, three hazards, live physics parameters, and a 500 ms observation window.
The generator creates ordered switches, walls, hazards, waypoints, physics, and minimum tick/control-change requirements for the approved baseline.
The visible board advances on physics ticks and records momentum, wall hits, wells, ordered lamp activation, and completion.
The approved grader binds simplified compass versus full analog input and deterministically replays every tilt tick, collision, reset, and completion requirement.
The reliquary baseline's source-selected L3 parameters are independently stated as six views, three wards, a four-digit clue, a five-colour clue, and combined construction.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 candy task requires four valid adjacent swaps whose cascades refill and change the board after each accepted move, while exact score, wave, licorice, and final-board constraints are replayed. The reliquary's baseline has a longer prescribed object-and-clue chain but no evolving board, physics, or branching route after each accepted action. This is a substantially harder state-changing planning anchor than the current static baseline, while not implying that the reliquary's own L5 profile must be relabeled across environments.

evidence.explanation: The approved L5 candy baseline is simplified interaction with four changing-board swaps, at least seven cascade waves, a five-item preview, and exact-change grading.
The candy generator resolves repeated matches/refills and enumerates routes recursively, passing the resulting board and refill cursor to the next swap.
The visible candy UI changes the board after each valid swap, resolves successive waves, updates score, and terminates on exact or over-budget outcomes.
The approved grader replays every swap and refill, checks the final board and score, rejects forbidden candy, and requires the exact valid-move budget and cascade threshold.

visible_baseline_solution: A screenshot-only agent starts at the door and uses the visible edge arrows to cycle through six fixed views. It must recognize the pictured but deliberately unmarked room objects, click the desk label frame, collect the revealed empty frame, open the cabinet lens drawer, collect the lens, combine the two tray objects by dragging, and drag the resulting loupe to the revealed label back to expose the digit clue. It removes the gallery dust sheet to expose the colour sequence, lifts the cabinet floor tile to collect the handle, collects the radiator wire, combines handle and wire into the hook, and drags the hook to the reliquary grate to recover the ward key. Returning to the door, it opens the digit and colour panels, enters the visible clues in forward order, drags the ward key to the keyhole, and clicks the door handle. The visible UI supplies the task instruction, fixed-view index, lock plates and wrong-entry counters, scene artwork, inventory cards, revealed clue values, and lock controls; the needed facts are spread across views and become available only after prerequisite actions. Full mode adds direct drag control and requires a real drag from the visible tray to another card or scene geometry, while simplified mode selects a tray object and then clicks the destination. A wrong code or key use can reach the three-strike seizure/reissued-challenge recovery path. Success is all active wards released followed by the door-handle action; the grader replays the ordered state transitions and geometry rather than trusting the submitted final state.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current baseline is exactly the generator's six-view, three-ward, four-digit, five-colour, combined-hook configuration with unmarked cues. It is materially above the approved L1 Isometric Voxel Extraction Mine in cross-view dependency, clue memory, and latent-affordance exploration, though it lacks that anchor's 3D raycast and finite-tool control. It is comparable to the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board on overall multi-stage burden but trades continuous physics and temporal motor correction for static inventory planning. It remains below the approved L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade in evolving-state planning: reliquary actions reveal a mostly prescribed dependency graph and do not force repeated choice on a changed world. The source therefore supports keeping L3/full provisionally, without treating the label as empirically calibrated.

evidence.explanation: The controls explicitly select difficulty 3/full and define the five configurations plus their two input surfaces.
The unconditioned generator baseline is six fixed roles with digit, colour, and key wards and combined construction.
The baseline target graph contains the frame/lens loupe chain, colour reveal, handle/wire hook chain, grate/key chain, and two code answers.
The browser implements the dependent scene actions, combinations, item uses, lock submissions, and three-strike seizure.
The independent grader replays fixed-view topology, availability flags, inventory, drag/input sources, clue-gated submissions, wards, and door completion.

uncertainties: No VNC, human, or computer-use-agent calibration was run, so absolute L3 difficulty and completion-time separation remain provisional.
Source inspection establishes unmarked transparent hotspots and generated hit rectangles but cannot establish their screenshot legibility at the runtime viewport.
The snapshot contains the current unconditioned task and controls, not a historical pre-controls implementation.

profiles.visible_problem: Three fixed views contain one digit ward and the frame/lens loupe chain. Clear cues mark the usable pictured objects. The agent turns with visible buttons, selects a tray object, and clicks a second tray object or its scene destination.
profiles.success_condition: Flip the label, collect the empty frame and lens, combine them into the loupe, use the loupe on the label code, enter the exact three-digit clue at the door, and click the door handle. There is no colour or key ward; three wrong digit submissions seize the run.
profiles.rationale: This is the smallest active dependency graph: one clue and one two-item construction across three views. It requires state tracking and exploration but has no second clue, key chain, cross-view direction, or distractors.

evidence.explanation: The L1 parameters specify three views, one three-digit lock, no colour clue, no hook, no decoys, and clear cues.
The generated three-view graph includes the door, desk, cabinet, and the frame/lens prerequisites.
The desk and cabinet render the clue-reveal and lens-discovery states used by the visible route.

profiles.visible_problem: The same three-view, one-digit-ward problem and visible clue discovery apply. The agent turns through edge arrows and directly drags inventory cards onto the other card or scene geometry.
profiles.success_condition: The success state is identical to simplified L1: reveal and enter the exact three-digit clue and open the door; three wrong submissions seize the run.
profiles.rationale: Full mode changes the motor surface, not the generated dependency graph, clue information, goal, or action effects. The drag must satisfy the direct-manipulation geometry contract, which is a control demand rather than a new difficulty stage.

evidence.explanation: The control pair defines simplified selection/clicking and full direct dragging for the same environment.
The full and simplified renderings differ in turn controls and inventory instruction while rendering the same state.
The grader selects mode-specific turn/combine/use input sources and validates a drag proof only for full mode.

profiles.visible_problem: Four fixed views add the gallery and a separately revealed four-colour clue. The existing loupe chain remains, and the agent uses turn buttons, selection, and clicks with clear object cues.
profiles.success_condition: Reveal the three-digit and four-colour clues, enter both exact values at the door in forward order, and click the door handle. No key construction is active; each active lock seizes after three wrong entries.
profiles.rationale: The added gallery is not an independent repeated action: it adds a second state-dependent clue and a second exact lock that must be remembered and solved after returning to the door.

evidence.explanation: L2 changes the view count to four and activates a four-colour ward while retaining clear cues and no hook.
The four-view role list adds the gallery, and the colour ward adds a dust-sheet target with a prerequisite-free reveal.
The gallery visibly changes from the dust sheet to the colour clue after the reveal action.

profiles.visible_problem: The four-view two-clue problem is unchanged. The agent turns through edge arrows and drags tray objects directly, while clue reveals and the two door entries remain the same.
profiles.success_condition: Reveal and remember both clues, enter the exact three-digit and four-colour values, and open the door; no key ward is active.
profiles.rationale: The full input surface adds drag precision only; the generator, revealed information, state transitions, and replayed goal are the L2 simplified equivalents.

evidence.explanation: The L2 world parameters are independent of the interaction choice.
Full mode binds edge arrows and direct card drags; simplified mode binds selection and click proxies, with the same scene and lock handlers.
The grader requires the selected interaction mode and maps only the input-source contract to that mode.

profiles.visible_problem: Six unmarked fixed views contain three wards, the loupe chain, the colour reveal, and a second handle/wire-to-hook chain. The agent turns with buttons and selects objects before clicking a second object or an applicable scene target; clue values must be carried back to the door.
profiles.success_condition: Complete both combinations, reveal both clues, recover the ward key through the hook and grate, enter the exact four-digit and five-colour values, use the key on the keyhole, and click the door handle. Any active lock can seize after three wrong entries.
profiles.rationale: This is the source-selected medium configuration: multiple state-dependent discoveries and two construction chains across six views, plus memory of two clues, but no cross-view direction card or evolving physical world.

evidence.explanation: The L3 profile activates six views, three wards, four/five-length clues, combined hook construction, and unmarked cues.
The combined branch creates floor, handle, radiator wire, grate, keyhole, and two recipes.
The browser applies recipe and item-use state transitions, including hook-to-key and key-to-ward effects.

profiles.visible_problem: The six-view, three-ward dependency graph is unchanged. The agent uses edge arrows and direct tray-to-card or tray-to-scene drags, with the same unmarked scene geometry and clue displays.
profiles.success_condition: The same two clues, two recipes, ward-key recovery, three ward releases, and door-handle completion are required.
profiles.rationale: Full L3 adds a genuine motor/geometry requirement to inventory manipulation but does not add world state, information, timing, tolerances, or success requirements; it remains the same difficulty profile for this audit.

evidence.explanation: The generated challenge hash uses the seed and difficulty parameters, not interaction mode; clues and answers are generated before the interaction condition is copied into both states.
Both modes render the same state and scene; only turn controls and the inventory instruction/interaction surface change.
Full mode's extra drag proof is checked for combinations and uses, while the state effect and success replay remain the same.

profiles.visible_problem: The L3 dependency graph remains, but a reliquary order-drawer discovery reveals a direction card for the digit and colour clues. The door lock dialogs are disabled until that card is revealed; the agent must remember each raw clue and reverse it when the card shows a left arrow. Turns and inventory actions use simplified buttons and selection.
profiles.success_condition: In addition to the L3 route, reveal the order card before submitting the digit and colour wards, apply its per-clue forward/reverse directions exactly, recover and use the key, and open the door.
profiles.rationale: cross_view_order changes the decision problem rather than adding a quota: it introduces a new required discovery and a state gate, then requires retaining two clue values and their separate reading directions while navigating back to the door.

evidence.explanation: L4 activates cross-view order while holding the L3 view, ward, clue, hook, cue, and seizure parameters constant.
Cross-view order randomly selects forward or reverse directions and computes answers from those directions.
The order parameter adds a separate order-drawer target in the reliquary view.
The visible order card renders a distinct arrow for each clue after the drawer is opened.
The digit and colour submissions are visibly disabled until the order card is revealed.

profiles.visible_problem: The six-view direction-card problem is unchanged. The agent uses edge arrows and direct drags for the two combinations and item applications; the order card and lock gate remain visible state requirements.
profiles.success_condition: Reveal and apply the two reading directions, release all three wards, and open the door with the same goal and seizure rule as simplified L4.
profiles.rationale: The full drag surface adds motor precision but does not alter the direction-card dependency, clues, effects, or success condition.

evidence.explanation: Full direct manipulation and simplified selection are bound to the same available scene targets and item state.
The replay requires clue evidence and order evidence before accepting either code, independently of the inventory input surface.
Mode-specific drag validation and the same key-misuse/seizure state are applied during full-mode replay.

profiles.visible_problem: The L4 six-view direction-card and two construction chains remain. The digit clue is now five characters and the colour clue six beads; the gallery and radiator also contain two plausible but harmless decoy objects. Simplified mode still uses selection and clicks.
profiles.success_condition: Reveal the direction card and both longer clues, enter the exact five-digit and six-colour values in their required directions, recover and use the key, and open the door. The decoys are collectible but not required for success.
profiles.rationale: The longer exact sequences increase both visual memory and controlled entry, and decoys add search ambiguity. The source does not add another state-dependent decision: the decoys can be ignored and the grader does not require every collectible, so this is the highest named profile but the weakest adjacent separation.

evidence.explanation: L5 changes only the L4 clue lengths and decoy count while retaining the six views, three wards, combined hook, unmarked cues, and order card.
The two decoy targets are appended as wax seal and bone pin, while the actual recipe graph remains the same two combinations.
The pass predicate requires completed replay and no seizure; collectible counts are reported but do not require all collectible objects.

profiles.visible_problem: The L5 six-view, longer-clue, direction-card problem is unchanged. The agent turns through edge arrows and directly drags cards for both combinations and scene uses; the optional decoy objects remain visible.
profiles.success_condition: Use the visible route to enter both exact longer clues, release all three wards, use the key, and click the door handle. Decoy collection is not part of the pass condition.
profiles.rationale: Full L5 adds the same direct-manipulation precision requirement as the other full profiles without changing the L5 generated world, clue information, action effects, or success predicate.

evidence.explanation: The challenge identity is derived from the seed and parameters, so interaction mode is not part of the generated world hash.
Full L5 uses direct drag bindings and simplified L5 uses selection bindings, both over the same target and lock handlers.
The grader rejects a transcript with the other mode's interaction label and chooses the expected source contract.

adjacent_pairs.full_change: Add the same two views and dependent key chain while retaining full edge-arrow and drag controls.

The key profile creates floor, handle, wire, grate, keyhole, and optional order targets with prerequisites.

evidence.explanation: The only difficulty-parameter change is cross_view_order false to true; the source keeps the same views, wards, clue lengths, hook, cues, and seizure count.

adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: Weakest but still source-distinguishable: exact entry grows from 4/5 to 5/6 values and the visual search set grows, but decoys are optional and add no new dependent decision. Empirical calibration is needed before treating the gap as a robust L4/L5 separation.

The added wax seal and bone pin are separate collectible targets, while the recipe graph is unchanged.

baseline_preservation.current_default_equivalence: Supported at the fixed-seed generated-world level. The unconditioned task uses the generator's BASELINE_PARAMETERS, whose values match the explicit difficulty-3 parameters, and its natural-language instruction matches the L3 profile. The generator's challenge hash uses the seed and parameter dictionary rather than interaction mode, so the explicit L3/full materialization preserves generated views, target geometry, clues, directions, recipes, and answers. The controlled task necessarily has a rewritten task identity and control-condition metadata.
baseline_preservation.historical_preservation: Not established. The supplied snapshot shows the current unconditioned task and current control implementation but no historical pre-controls implementation; previous audits and reviews were not consulted.

evidence.explanation: The generator's unconditioned baseline parameters are the same values as controlled L3.
A controlled task uses its difficulty parameters, while an unconditioned task falls back to BASELINE_PARAMETERS.
The stable challenge identity and generated clues are derived from seed and difficulty parameters; interaction is not included in that generation hash.
Public and hidden states receive the same generated world and answers, and controlled tasks copy the condition into both.
Materialization copies the base task, preserves or replaces its natural-language instruction from the selected profile, and adds the controlled condition.
The browser defaults an unconditioned task to full interaction, matching the selected baseline.

missing_evidence: A pre-controls source revision or frozen historical task artifact.
A fixed-seed behavioral snapshot comparing the historical task with the current explicit L3/full materialization.
Historical human or agent calibration for the baseline.

interaction_equivalence.physics_timing_tolerances: Static synchronous behavior and target geometry are shared; only full drag proof adds a surface-specific gesture requirement.
interaction_equivalence.success: Both require both exact wards and the same door-handle action.
interaction_equivalence.input_grading_surface_binding: Browser handlers and replay use the mode-specific button/selection versus edge-arrow/drag sources; a transcript from the other mode is rejected.

evidence.explanation: The L2 parameters do not vary by interaction mode.

interaction_equivalence.world: Both modes use the same six-view, three-ward, combined-hook generated condition.
interaction_equivalence.information: Both expose the same unmarked artwork, dependent discoveries, four-digit and five-colour clues, recipes, and lock panels.
interaction_equivalence.effects: Both share every scene flag, inventory change, recipe output, clue reveal, ward release, seizure, and exit effect.
interaction_equivalence.physics_timing_tolerances: No physical simulation or timed action is active. Generated target rectangles and grader click/drag tolerances are common; full additionally validates drag travel and samples.
interaction_equivalence.success: Both require the same three wards and final door handle, with final state independently replayed.
interaction_equivalence.input_grading_surface_binding: Simplified browser events are buttons/selections and full browser events are edge arrows/drags; the payload mode and each input_source are checked by the grader.

evidence.explanation: The same L5 difficulty parameters are paired with both implemented interaction modes.
The two surface bindings invoke the same scene/item actions and lock controls.
The grader rejects mismatched interaction_mode and establishes separate expected input sources.

findings.claim: The source supports a higher L5 profile, but 4->5 is the least structurally separated adjacent pair.
findings.causal_explanation: L5 lengthens the two exact entries and adds two visible decoys. The decoys are harmless collectibles and the grader's pass predicate does not require collecting them, so an agent can follow the same required dependency graph as L4 and ignore them. The remaining change is meaningful memory and entry control, but source inspection cannot show that it produces a robust empirical L4/L5 gap.

evidence.explanation: The L4-to-L5 parameter delta is only clue length and two decoys.
Decoys are appended as optional target/collectible branches and do not modify either required recipe.
Passing checks completed replay and no seizure, while collectible totals are only reported.

findings.recommended_action: Keep the pair provisionally, then use held-out human and computer-use-agent calibration to decide whether the source-supported length/clutter increase separates L4 from L5.

findings.claim: The generated browser public state contains exact digit and colour answers under runtime_lock_answers, and the browser uses that field for acceptance.
findings.causal_explanation: An agent allowed to inspect page state could bypass the clue-discovery and direction-memory burden by reading the answer field, and the cheat endpoint also exposes answers. This is not a screenshot-visible bypass and is outside the required screenshot-only protocol, but it is an implementation boundary that must not be confused with normal visual difficulty.

evidence.explanation: public_state includes raw clues, directions, and runtime_lock_answers.
The browser compares submitted guesses directly with state.runtime_lock_answers.
The grader intentionally binds the public runtime answers to hidden truth and validates them against the raw clues and directions.

findings.recommended_action: Make no change for this screenshot-only audit; preserve the visible-task-only evaluation boundary and do not treat public browser play as a secret evaluation surface.

findings.claim: The generator accepts cue_level subtle and hook_mode ready, but no frozen profile activates either; max_wrong_entries is fixed at three in every profile.
findings.causal_explanation: These branches are implementation-supported options rather than active difficulty variables for this ten-configuration audit. They must not receive difficulty credit or be used to justify the current profile ordering.

evidence.explanation: Validation supports ready, subtle, and a fixed seizure value of exactly three.
The frozen profiles use only none/combined hook modes, clear/unmarked cues, and max_wrong_entries three.
The ready-hook branch exists, while the controlled profiles use no hook or combined construction.

findings.recommended_action: Do not credit these inactive branches in the ten profiles; introduce them only as separately calibrated configurations if needed.

concise_summary: Keep the current After Hours at the Reliquary L3/full baseline and the five-level ordering provisionally. The source shows real state-dependent exploration and memory through L3, a required direction-card step at L4, and longer exact clues at L5. The L4-to-L5 separation is weakest because decoys are optional, and browser state contains answers outside the screenshot-only protocol. No runtime checks were performed.
limitations: No browser, VNC, human, or computer-use-agent calibration was performed.
No multi-seed generation or exported-verifier check was performed; the parent performs those checks separately.
Screenshot legibility of the deliberately unmarked transparent hotspots and empirical L4/L5 separation remain unverified.
Historical pre-controls preservation cannot be assessed from the supplied snapshot.
